item.case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
item.title: Meet the Real F-35A

turns.text: Make an 8-second widescreen mini-documentary introducing the real F-35A Lightning II. Show it taking off from a runway, then flying. Label it 'F-35A Lightning II', with 'One engine' and 'Conventional takeoff' appearing in turn. Calm English narration explaining those two facts. Real aircraft proportions, not a sci-fi jet.

item.tests: Tests whether a short factual aircraft film preserves the named variant's visible geometry and operating characteristics.

answer_sheet.Aircraft and variant: The real F-35A Lightning II, not the F-35B or F-35C.
answer_sheet.On-screen wording: F-35A Lightning II; One engine; Conventional takeoff.
answer_sheet.Narration: Calm English narration explaining that the F-35A has one engine and takes off conventionally from a runway; exact wording and voice are your call.
answer_sheet.Visual style and setting: Realistic documentary imagery; runway location, weather and camera angles are your call.
answer_sheet.Music: Your call, provided the narration remains clear.

must_haves: The aircraft has the recognizable F-35 configuration: one rear engine exhaust, two outward-canted vertical tails and no canards.
The takeoff shows a forward runway roll and lift-off, not hovering or a vertical launch.
The same aircraft design remains consistent between the runway and airborne views.
All three requested labels appear exactly and are legible.
Audible English narration correctly describes one engine and conventional runway takeoff without attributing F-35B hover capability to the F-35A.

turns.text: Make an 8-second widescreen mini-documentary introducing the real F-35A Lightning II. Show it taking off from a runway, then flying, with realistic aircraft proportions—not a sci-fi jet. Label it 'F-35A Lightning II', and have 'One engine' and 'Conventional takeoff' appear in turn. Include calm English narration explaining that it has one engine and takes off conventionally from a runway. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**Nothing has been generated or charged.** I’ve only used the free planning tools.

For your **8-second, widescreen (16:9), 480p** video, the planner quotes:

| Component | Credits |
|---|---:|
| Runway takeoff + flight footage, 8 seconds total | 192 |
| Separately generated calm English narration | 192 |
| Joining the clips and narration | 0 |
| **Total** | **384** |

These settings use free-plan-compatible models. This is a planning quote—not verification of your available balance.

**Cheaper options**
- **4 seconds, with separate narration:** 192 credits, but takeoff, flight and three labels would feel rushed.
- **8 seconds, with narration generated alongside the footage:** potentially **192 credits** using LTX-2.5, whose audio has no extra credit charge. Timing and spoken wording are less controlled.
- **Smaller:** 480p is already the lowest supported resolution for these free-plan video models.

Suggested narration:
> “The F-35A Lightning II has one engine and takes off conventionally from a runway.”

Two limitations: generated footage can get aircraft geometry wrong, and generated labels can be misspelled. Exact text cards are more reliable, but take time away from the aircraft footage.

**Would you prefer the 384-credit separate-narration version or the cheaper 192-credit integrated-audio attempt?** For the labels, would you prefer text over the footage with possible spelling errors, or exact standalone cards?
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with that—the cheaper 192-credit, 8-second integrated-audio version. Use exact standalone cards for the labels.

turns.agent:
Magic Hour refused the request with **“insufficient credits.”** The tool reports that **nothing was created**, so I stopped without attempting more generations.

The revised eight-second version was quoted at **144 credits**, including exact standalone cards and six seconds of footage with integrated narration.

A shorter four-second version—two one-second cards plus two seconds of footage—would cost **48 credits**, but would be too rushed for clear narration and both aircraft actions. I haven’t run it or verified whether your balance covers it.
